key_decisions.rationale: Retains gendered sequence and ambiguous head metaphor.
key_decisions.before: Yet I want you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, the head of a woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.
key_decisions.after: But I want you to know that Christ is the head of every man, the man is the head of a woman, and God is the head of Christ.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But I want you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, the head of a woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves male worship activity and disputed covering description.
key_decisions.before: Every man who prays or prophesies with something on his head disgraces his head.
key_decisions.after: Every man who prays or prophesies with something hanging down from his head dishonors his head.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Every man who prays or prophesies with something on his head disgraces his head.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps women's active worship and shame comparison.
key_decisions.before: But every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered disgraces her head—it is one and the same as if her head were shaved.
key_decisions.after: But every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is one and the same as having her head shaved.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered disgraces her head—it is one and the same as if her head were shaved.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains gender-specific claims without smoothing them.
key_decisions.before: For a man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but woman is the glory of man.
key_decisions.after: For a man ought not cover his head, since he is God's image and glory, but woman is man's glory.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For a man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but woman is the glory of man.

key_decisions.rationale: Renders authority positively and retains angelic rationale.
key_decisions.before: For this reason a woman ought to have authority over her head, because of the angels.
key_decisions.after: For this reason, and because of the angels, a woman ought to have authority over her head.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For this reason a woman ought to have authority over her head, because of the angels.

key_decisions.before: Even so, in the Lord woman is not independent of man, nor man independent of woman.
key_decisions.after: Nevertheless, in the Lord woman is not independent of man, nor man independent of woman.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Nevertheless, in the Lord woman is not independent of man, nor man independent of woman.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves origin reversal and divine source.
key_decisions.before: For just as woman came from man, so also man is born through woman—and everything are from God.
key_decisions.after: For just as woman came from man, so man is born through woman, and all things come from God.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For just as woman came from man, so also man is born through woman—and all things are from God.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves Paul's nature claim and continuing contrast.

key_decisions.after: Does not nature itself teach you that if a man wears long hair, it is a dishonor to him,

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves dispute-closing appeal to communal practice.

key_decisions.after: But if anyone is inclined to be contentious, we have no other practice, nor do God's churches.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves ironic negation of their meal.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps socioeconomic harm and repeated refusal to praise.

key_decisions.tsw_comparator: What! Do you not have houses to eat and drink in? Or do you despise the church of God and shame those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? In this I do not praise you.
